evals.prompt: I have a FASTA file of 40 plasmid constructs (plasmid_constructs.fasta) I need to load into our Benchling registry. Write a script that creates each as a circular DNA sequence in folder fld_abc123 and registers it.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling. Uses the benchling-sdk Python client (Benchling + ApiKeyAuth), parsing the FASTA with Bio.SeqIO; for a 40-sequence load it builds the request models and registers them — ideally one dna_sequences.bulk_create job with DnaSequenceBulkCreate items (the skill's documented path for many sequences), or dna_sequences.create with DnaSequenceCreate per item — each with bases, is_circular=True, folder_id, and registry_id plus a naming_strategy given as the NamingStrategy enum (NamingStrategy.NEW_IDS or NamingStrategy.IDS_FROM_NAMES), not a bare string. Should not pass both entity_registry_id and naming_strategy together.

assertions.value: Uses benchling.dna_sequences.bulk_create (or .create) and registers by setting registry_id with a naming_strategy; does not combine entity_registry_id with naming_strategy in the same create call.

evals.prompt: Can you script an audit of every container in box box_abc123 in our Benchling inventory, printing each container's name and barcode?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling. Uses benchling.containers.list(ancestor_storage_id=...) (list() has no parent_storage_id filter) and iterates the paginated generator (for page in ...: for container in page) printing container.name and container.barcode, following the inventory-management capability.

assertions.value: Iterates the Benchling containers list generator page-by-page rather than assuming a flat list.

evals.prompt: I want to run a SQL query against our Benchling Data Warehouse to aggregate experimental results by schema and pull them into a Jupyter notebook for analysis.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling. Routes to the Data Warehouse & Analytics capability: connect to the Benchling Data Warehouse via a standard SQL client with provided credentials, run the aggregation query, and load results into Jupyter for analysis.

evals.prompt: Automate creating a Benchling ELN entry for today's experiment and open a PCR Amplification workflow task assigned to a teammate.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling. Uses benchling.entries.create_entry with EntryCreate and benchling.workflow_tasks.create with WorkflowTaskCreate (workflow_task_group_id, assignee_id, fields), covering the notebook and workflow capabilities.

assertions.value: Creates an ELN entry and a workflow task via the benchling-sdk entries and workflow_tasks services.

evals.prompt: Before anything touches our Benchling tenant, build the bulk-create payload for the constructs in constructs.fasta (circular, folder lib_K9t2Qx, registered into registry src_7Hc1Ld with new registry IDs) and validate it offline. Show me the exact JSON body for the first construct and tell me which records would cause trouble.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling on the keyless path, with no Benchling account or API key: builds DnaSequenceBulkCreate models (benchling-sdk) from the five FASTA records with is_circular=True, folder_id='lib_K9t2Qx', registry_id='src_7Hc1Ld' and naming_strategy=NamingStrategy.NEW_IDS (the enum, not a string), and serializes them offline with .to_dict(). Shows the first body for pGFP-01 with camelCase keys (name, bases, isCircular: true, folderId, registryId, namingStrategy: NEW_IDS). Flags pRFP-03 because its bases contain U (an RNA base, not valid in a DNA sequence) and the second pGFP-02 record as a duplicate name, so three of the five records are clean. Ends with the bulk_create call to run later with the user's own BENCHLING_API_KEY, without claiming anything was created.

assertions.value: Flags pRFP-03 for containing U and the repeated pGFP-02 name, shows the serialized camelCase body for pGFP-01, and does not claim any entity was created in a tenant.

evals.prompt: A postdoc wrote register_plasmids.py for our Benchling tenant. Before I give it our API key, review it against the current benchling-sdk and tell me every line that will fail or misbehave, with the corrected call.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling and reviews the script offline against benchling-sdk 1.x without running it on a tenant: (1) naming_strategy='NEW_IDS' must be NamingStrategy.NEW_IDS — a plain string fails when the request is serialized; (2) entity_registry_id and naming_strategy are set together, which is not allowed — use one; (3) benchling.containers.transfer does not exist — moving a tube is containers.update(...) with a new parent_storage_id (or transfer_into_container to move contents); (4) containers.list has no parent_storage_id filter — use ancestor_storage_id; (5) there is no wait_for_task helper — bulk_create returns a TaskHelper, call task.wait_for_response(). Gives the corrected code.

assertions.value: Identifies all five defects (string naming_strategy, entity_registry_id together with naming_strategy, nonexistent containers.transfer, parent_storage_id list filter, nonexistent wait_for_task) and supplies corrected calls.

evals.prompt: I exported our Benchling inventory to containers_export.csv. Which non-archived tubes in box FRZ-A1 are below 50 ng/uL or have no barcode, and how many micrograms of pGFP-01 DNA do we hold in non-archived tubes? Then give me the SDK script that would pull the same report live next time.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-benchling and answers from the exported CSV offline, with no Benchling account. In FRZ-A1, excluding the archived GFP-prep-05: below 50 ng/uL are GFP-prep-02 (41), RFP-prep-01 (23) and GFP-prep-06 (35); GFP-prep-03 has no barcode (LAC-prep-02 also lacks one but is in FRZ-A2). pGFP-01 in non-archived tubes: 182x50 + 41x45 + 35x15 ng = 11,470 ng = 11.47 ug in 110 uL. Then provides a live version using benchling.containers.list(ancestor_storage_id=...) iterated page by page, noting it runs only with the user's own BENCHLING_API_KEY.

assertions.value: Lists GFP-prep-02, RFP-prep-01 and GFP-prep-06 as below 50 ng/uL and GFP-prep-03 as missing a barcode, excludes the archived GFP-prep-05, and reports about 11.47 ug of pGFP-01.

evals.prompt: I need to programmatically back up my LabArchives notebook as a 7z archive with all attachments and then push a Jupyter export into it as a new entry.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-labarchive. The platform is LabArchives (notebook_backup, entry_operations, Jupyter integration), not Benchling, so the LabArchives ELN skill is correct.

evals.prompt: Help me search protocols.io for a CRISPR-Cas9 protocol, create my own version with steps and materials, and publish it with a DOI.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-protocolsio. The user is managing protocols on protocols.io (search, steps/materials, DOI publishing via the protocols.io API v3/v4), not Benchling registry/inventory/ELN data.
